transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-05-09 16:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Sam Patel (Orion Head of Search), Maya Torres (Orion ML Eng), Ethan Wu (Orion CTO)

Summary: quick discovery to understand Orion's plan for adding reranking on top of embeddings, vector DB choices, throughput targets, and whether Hosted/Dedicated/Private fit their security posture.

Topics: embeddings dimensionality, vector DB integration (current stack: Elastic + custom FAISS), hybrid search (BM25 + ANN), throughput/ingest, quantization, data residency/VPC, benchmark plan.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'll kick off. Uh, this is Jordan from Redwood AE, with Priya SE — thanks for making time today. Can you do quick intros?
[00:12] Sam: Sam here, head of search at Orion. We're re-architecting search for analytics product, currently using Elastic for indexing and a homegrown FAISS service for dense retrieval.
[00:20] Maya: Maya, ML eng, working on feature extraction and embeddings pipeline.
[00:25] Ethan: Ethan, CTO, listening in for scale and security Qs.
[00:30] Priya: nice to meet you all, I'll focus on technical fit — latency/throughput and integration patterns.
[00:36] Jordan: high level — you're looking at embeddings + rerank. What's the expected scale? docs, qps, dims?
[00:42] Sam: goal is about 3–5 million docs initially, 10M in 6 months. Query load is bursty — 3k to 5k qps during reporting windows, but avg ~500 qps. Current embeddings are 768-dim (we train on a custom encoder) but we can go to 1024 if needed.
[00:58] Maya: latency SLO is 200–300ms P95 for the retrieval + rerank step end-to-end. Rerank model is smaller cross-encoder we run as a second-stage.
[01:10] Jordan: got it. So you currently use Elastic for text + FAISS for dense, and then a cross-encoder for rerank?
[01:15] Sam: yeah. The FAISS infra is brittle, ops heavy, and doesn't have good autoscaling for bursts. We're evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs on-prem/private because of both cost and data residency.
[01:25] Priya: quick Q — how important is hybrid search (BM25 + embeddings) vs pure ANN?
[01:30] Sam: hybrid is important for some enterprise customers — title/metadata matches still need BM25. We want a pipeline that supports hybrid scoring (bm25 + dot/cosine) and then rerank on top.
[01:40] Priya: Redwood supports hybrid patterns — you can do routed queries to an Elastic/OpenSearch step or use our built-in re-ranking flow. For vector stores, what vendors are you evaluating?
[01:49] Maya: Pinecone and Milvus were shortlisted, we also have folks testing Weaviate. We're curious whether Redwood can integrate with existing Elastic or replace FAISS.
[02:00] Jordan: Redwood Hosted has managed vector capabilities and integrations; Dedicated gives you guaranteed GPU capacity if you want to run models close to the vectors; Private lets you run in VPC/on-prem with customer KMS. Tradeoffs are cost vs control.
[02:12] Ethan: security-wise we need SOC2, SSO, audit logs, and a VPC option. Some customers require that vectors never leave our VPC.
[02:20] Priya: we support SAML/SSO, audit logs, and Private deployment for VPC/on-prem where control plane is in your environment. For Hosted we offer encryption at rest and customer KMS support as an add-on for enterprise.
[02:33] Sam: great. On throughput — how do you see sustained insert throughput for 5–10M docs and qps during bursts? Also indexing speed — we do nightly batches of ~500k embeddings.
[02:44] Priya: for Dedicated, we size GPU pools to handle both ingestion and queries. Typical datapoints: on x1-type (example) node you can do ~100–200k embeddings per hour depending on model and batching; for ANN search HNSW latency at 768 dims is sub-2ms per query at small scales but depends on ef/search settings and replica count. For our Hosted vector index, we have autoscaling but burst limits apply — we can provide a burst SLA in Dedicated.
[03:10] Maya: can you clarify dims — 768 vs 1024 vs 1536 — how does that affect cost/latency?
[03:16] Priya: higher dimensionality increases vector-memory and ANN index size roughly linearly, so search latencies and RAM for HNSW increase. For example, 1536-dim vectors will use ~2x memory of 768-dim and may increase CPU/GPU time for distance computations; we recommend quantization for storage and CPU-optimized ANN for cheaper lookups if recall allows it.
[03:38] Jordan: also important — whether you run embedding generation on Redwood or push precomputed vectors. What's your current flow?
[03:44] Maya: we compute embeddings in our pipeline and store them. We'd prefer to keep embedding generation inside our infra for data control, but open to Redwood-hosted inference if latency/cost wins are clear.
[03:55] Priya: we support both: push precomputed vectors via bulk ingest APIs and live embed generation via our model serving. For POC it's common to push precomputed vectors to eliminate model variability.
[04:07] Sam: about reranking — we plan to use a cross-encoder that takes top-100 candidates and reranks to top-10. Can Redwood host that reranker near the index for lower tail latency?
[04:18] Priya: yes, on Dedicated you can colocate reranker on the same cluster or a low-latency tier. For Hosted we can route to a low-latency variant but the strictest control is with Dedicated/Private.
[04:29] Ethan: curious about cost math — do you have guidance vs running FAISS ourselves? We're trying to model TCO over 1 year.
[04:35] Jordan: typical levers — Dedicated reserved capacity reduces per-token/ per-query cost; caches (prefix/KV) and batching reduce compute for embedding generation. If you run FAISS self-hosted you save on vendor cost but pay more ops and variability. We'll send a sizing worksheet to plug numbers.
[04:49] Maya: any limitations on vector dimension for your managed indexes?
[04:53] Priya: no hard limit; we recommend 768–1536. Higher dims OK but need careful memory planning.
[04:59] Sam: what about hybrid search — can Redwood do vector+BM25 in single query path?
[05:04] Priya: two patterns: use a hybrid index (some customers push dense vectors into a vector index that also stores doc text and run a combined scoring) or run staged queries — BM25 first (fast), then ANN, then unify scores and rerank. We have built-in support for both via our query orchestration and ranking API.
[05:20] Jordan: we've seen teams prefer staged pipeline for more control and explainability, especially with enterprise constraints.
[05:26] Maya: for the POC we want to measure recall lift and latency. Sample success criteria: +15% recall@10 on core queries, P95 end-to-end under 300ms, cost < X.
[05:36] Priya: sounds reasonable. We typically recommend a benchmark plan — 5M docs, 768-dim embeddings, run 1k sustained qps with 5k peak bursts, evaluate recall/latency.
[05:48] Sam: what about ANN algorithm choices? HNSW vs IVF-PQ vs ScaNN? We currently use FAISS HNSW.
[05:56] Priya: HNSW is a solid default for high recall and low tail latency. IVF-PQ or PQ + quantization reduces memory and often used at very large scale. We can test multiple index types during POC.
[06:07] Ethan: any caveats around consistency/replication during index builds? If we bulk ingest 500k/day, how is index rebuilt or merged?
[06:15] Priya: we support background index merges and partial updates. For Dedicated, you can provision a separate ingest cluster to avoid impacting query tier, or use index streaming to add vectors incrementally.
[06:27] Sam: do you expose metrics we can scrape? We want per-query latency, tokens, index size, ef/search settings.
[06:33] Priya: yes, Redwood Console has dashboards with per-route latency, token breakdowns, index size, memory, and we provide tracing hooks. Export via Prometheus for ops teams is supported on Dedicated/Private.
[06:45] Jordan: some customers ask about quantized serving — product question: do you do 8-bit or 4-bit quantized ANN?
[06:53] Priya: for model inference we support quantized kernels for LLMs (4/8-bit) and for vector storage we support PQ/OPQ and scalar quantization depending on index type. This reduces memory at cost of recall.
[07:05] Maya: any example tradeoffs? like recall vs memory?
[07:09] Priya: typical: moving from full-float to PQ can drop recall by 2–6% depending on workload, but reduce memory by 3–8x. We'll measure on your dataset.
[07:19] Sam: integration — what's the ingest API look like? bulk CSV, streaming?
[07:24] Priya: bulk ingest via multipart uploads or S3 connector, streaming ingest via SDKs. We also have connector patterns for Elastic to copy docs into Redwood indexes.
[07:35] Jordan: any customers in regulated industries doing Private on-prem for vectors?
[07:39] Priya: yes, a couple of healthcare and finance customers run Private with HSM for KMS and strict audit controls. That is usually Dedicated-level perf but with customer-controlled networking and storage.
[07:52] Ethan: about SLA — what's uptime and latency SLOs for Dedicated?
[07:57] Jordan: standard Dedicated SLA is 99.95% and latency targets depend on config; we'll include specific numbers in the pricing worksheet.
[08:06] Sam: request — we want to test 5M docs, 768 dims, top-100 rerank, 1k sustained qps, 5k peak bursts. Can Redwood run that as a 1-week POC?
[08:15] Priya: yes — typical POC pattern: we provision Dedicated burst capacity, run ingest and queries with your dataset, and measure recall/latency/cost. We'll provide a runbook and collect metrics.
[08:25] Maya: what telemetry will you collect?
[08:28] Priya: per-request latency, candidate set sizes, reranker latency, index memory, search ef settings, hit rates, and cost per query estimate.
[08:36] Sam: is there any vendor lock-in risk? If we later want to move index to Milvus or other, how portable are vectors and metadata?
[08:43] Priya: vectors and payloads are standard (embeddings + JSON metadata). You can export snapshots; index formats differ but vector blobs can be exported/imported. We'll provide migration docs.
[08:53] Jordan: ok let's talk timeline — we're aiming to start POC mid-May and evaluate by end of June. Next steps would be Jordan shares pricing and Priya shares benchmark runbook.
[09:03] Ethan: quick legal question — data retention and encryption in Hosted — can we require customer-managed keys?
[09:09] Priya: yes, enterprise Hosted plus KMS/HSM option; otherwise Private gives you full control.
[09:15] Sam: any gotchas with hybrid search explainability — customers want to see why results scored a certain way.
[09:22] Priya: we surface score breakdowns (BM25 score, vector distance, reranker score) and trace logs for debugging.
[09:30] Maya: performance question — how do you handle cold cache on burst windows?
[09:34] Priya: we pre-warm caches and have tiered memory. Dedicated lets you reserve hot slots and we can schedule prefetch during expected bursts.
[09:44] Jordan: ok, let's capture action items (brief).
[09:47] Sam: go ahead.
[09:48] Jordan: Jordan will send pricing and Dedicated sizing by Monday 2026-05-11. Priya will share POC runbook and proposed cluster size by Tuesday 2026-05-12. Sam will share dataset + queries by Tue 2026-05-12. We'll schedule follow-up to kick off benchmark week of 2026-05-18.
[10:05] Maya: one more — do you have examples of cost per 1k qps or per-embedding?
[10:10] Jordan: we have ballpark numbers; exact will be in worksheet. For 768-dim embeddings, Hosted vector ops are priced per-indexed vector + query unit; Dedicated shifts to reserved monthly pricing.
[10:22] Ethan: ok thanks, seems good.
[10:24] Jordan: great — thanks everyone, we'll follow up with notes and the runbook.
[10:28] Sam: thanks.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings: "FAISS" transcribed correctly most times but sometimes as "fess"; Redwood product names sometimes shortened to 'Dedicated' or 'Hosted' only. Some cross-talk and brief interruptions were present.

End of transcript.
